text:
Frank Nazar is the Blackhawk stepping into the hole. With Connor Bedard out with a shoulder injury, and the team weighing rehab or surgery, Scott Powers reports Nazar has taken Bedard's spot on the power play. He has earned the look: seven goals in his last 10 games, goals in three straight (two each against Buffalo and Toronto), and 10 on the season.

How much of it is real? Partly. His chances are up a little, but finishing is doing most of the work: 10 goals on 6.2 expected (the quality of his chances), shooting 27% after 11% last year. Balancing that, Chicago has scored 8.3 fewer goals than expected with him on the ice, and the team is seven points better in expected-goal share with him than without him.

The Detroit native has the tools to keep this going. He is fast, shoots hard (both around the 90th percentile by NHL Edge), and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck into the zone 62% of the time last season. Watch his assists: just two this year, which won't stay that low on the top power play.
